_comment: THE SHARED ASSET REGISTRY. One table naming every heavy test asset: where to look for it, and
-- the part that matters -- WHAT MAKES IT USABLE. Read by scripts/asset_registry.py (the sweep's
preflight) and by decoder/asset_registry_test.go (the gates). Both apply the SAME predicate to
the SAME candidate paths, because both read this file.
WHY IT EXISTS. The preflight reimplemented 'is this asset present' as `[ -e $path ]` while each
gate wrote its own resolution inline. Three consequences, all observed:
1. A directory satisfies `-e` -- so three preflight entries pointed at a DIRECTORY while the
loader wanted a .gguf FILE inside it, and preflight reported them resolved. Four gates were
costed by that.
2. GOINFER_QWEN35_GOLDEN's real requirement is a READABLE manifest.json INSIDE the directory.
`-e` on the directory cannot express that, so preflight said present and the gate skipped.
3. GOINFER_PREQUANT_GGUF had THREE different fallbacks across four call sites, and one site
(loadInt4Model) had none at all -- so the same box ran different gates against different
files, or skipped, with nothing in any output naming the difference.
THE PREDICATE, stated once so it cannot be reimplemented differently:
kind=file  -- resolves to a regular file (symlinks followed) of at least min_bytes.
kind=dir   -- resolves to a directory containing EVERY name in `members` and AT LEAST ONE
name in `members_any`.
The first candidate that satisfies the predicate wins. An `env` value set by the operator ALWAYS
wins over the candidates, and is checked by the same predicate -- an explicit path that does not
satisfy it is an error worth naming, not a silent fallback to something else.
$MODELS is $GOINFER_MODELS, defaulting to ~/models. $REPO is the goinfer checkout root.
used_by IS NOT DECORATION: TestAssetRegistry_usedByExists fails when a named gate does not exist,
so a renamed or deleted gate cannot leave a stale entry behind claiming coverage.

assets.note: q4_k_m GGUF; the loader dequantizes and re-quantizes, so no prebuilt .giw is needed. The $REPO candidate is a gitignored local drop and is tried FIRST so a developer copy beats the shared one.
members is the WHOLE point here: every consumer reads manifest.json out of this directory, so a directory that exists without one is NOT this asset.

Resolved in a file-level helper (realQwen35Dir) rather than in a test body, which is why the selector census attributed it inconsistently -- see B13's 42-vs-41 count. It was NOT in the sweep preflight before this registry.

The bf16 SAFETENSORS release, NOT the Q8_0 GGUF the coherence gate uses (GOINFER_GRANITE_GGUF, still unregistered). The T3 oracle must load the same weights the HF reference forward ran on, so these are two assets, not two paths to one.
The bf16 SAFETENSORS release, NOT the Q8_0 GGUF the coherence gate uses (GOINFER_NEMOTRON_GGUF, still unregistered).

z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash (apache-2.0, 0.77 GB) — the OUTLIER dialect: block_size NESTED in dflash_config and rope as nested rope_parameters, where the other three drafters use the top-level/flat spellings. Kept because it is the row of TestDFlash_pairingDialects that exercises those two spellings.

f32 conversion of deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7 (license=None; accepted for exploration 2026-08-15, see docs/prompts/dspark-license-issue.md), via scripts/convert_dflash_f32.py from $MODELS/dspark-qwen3-4b.
Qwen/Qwen3-4B (apache-2.0) — the TARGET z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16 is trained against. DFlash ships no embedding and no LM head, so the drafter cannot produce a token without it.

The f32 CONVERSION of z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16 (MIT), produced by scripts/convert_dflash_f32.py from $MODELS/qwen3-4b-dflash. The parity gate runs at f32 because the reference dump is f32; the bf16 original is not interchangeable here.

z-lab/gpt-oss-20b-DFlash (MIT, 1.57 GB) — pairs with our local gpt-oss-20b (hidden 2880, 24 layers, vocab 201088, all exact). NOTE the depth ratio: an 8-layer trunk against a 24-layer target is 0.33, far worse than the 4B's 5/32 = 0.156, and probe A established depth ratio is the mechanism — price this pairing as the expensive one.
z-lab/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-DFlash (apache-2.0, 0.86 GB) — pairs with our local gemma-4-26b-a4b-it (hidden 2816, 30 layers, vocab 262144, all exact).

Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (41 shards / 162.6 GB bf16) — the family's T3 oracle. The FULL checkpoint, not the 6-shard slice pulled 2026-08-17: a slice proves real weights at real distributions but not depth, and the T3 claim is about the whole model. goinfer loads it at int4 (~40 GB); int8 would be ~80 GB against 62 GB of RAM, so the quant is forced by capacity rather than chosen. The bf16 reference is NOT co-resident — scripts/pin_qwen3next_real.py pins it to testdata/qwen3next_real_golden.json first, through accelerate disk offload.

NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 (63 GB safetensors) — the MoE variant's T3 oracle. BF16 and not the -FP8 release: goinfer has no fp8 reader anywhere in the tree (the blocker that stopped DeepSeek V4-Flash scoping), so the FP8 repo is unusable here regardless of its smaller size.

Q4_K_M (24.7 GB) — the SAME quant the loader's expert dequantization was spot-checked against by hand, so the gate closes exactly the gap that check left open: correct dims and sane values are not a forward pass.

Real poolside Laguna-XS.2 (33B-A3B, bf16 safetensors, 14 shards, ~63GB). members lists the three files the gate actually reads besides the shards: config.json (the adapter), the shard INDEX (the loader resolves tensors through it, so a dir with shards but no index is not this asset), and tokenizer.json. Loaded at int4 -- bf16 would not fit alongside f32 activations in 62GB. There is deliberately NO M.1 entry: it is ~220B / ~400GB and not runnable here.

poolside's OWN Laguna-XS-2.1 Q4_K_M GGUF. llama.cpp has first-class laguna support (general.architecture == 'laguna'), so this is a released file rather than a local conversion. It exercises the fused+stacked expert layout, the per-layer head-count ARRAY, and the derived full/sliding split -- none of which the safetensors gate covers.

poolside/Laguna-XS.2-speculator.dflash -- the first VENDOR-BLESSED block drafter goinfer pairs with. Ships its own embed_tokens + reduced-vocab lm_head (32000 rows) + d2t, unlike z-lab's which borrow the target's head.
openai/gpt-oss-20b SAFETENSORS (MXFP4 experts as paired U8 *_blocks/*_scales, interleaved gate_up). Diffed against the GGUF of the same model, whose path is already T3-validated.
The validated-reader side of the safetensors diff. Same weights: its attn_norm matches the safetensors input_layernorm at max|diff| = 0.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, 18 bf16 shards / 55.6 GB. The whole multimodal repo is downloaded because the text decoder's shards are interleaved with the vision tower's; the loader requests neither model.visual.* nor mtp.*. Loaded at int4 -- Options{} would ask for the f32 dequant of a 27.8B model.

The MATCHED half of the W4A8 decode-parity pair. Both halves are built from the SAME source GGUF (~/models/qwen2.5-coder-1.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf, the model the test's own docstring names) so the pair is matched by construction: `go run ./cmd/prequant -quant int4 -o ~/models/qwen15-w4a8-int4.giw <src>` and the same with `-quant int8int8 -o ~/models/qwen15-w4a8-int8.giw`. Built 2026-08-18 to close the v1.0 gate's w4a8 coverage line; the gate passed 16/16 on first run. Rebuild both together or not at all -- an int4 half paired with an int8 half from a different source measures nothing.

unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF UD-Q4_K_M, 16.5 GB — the dense qwen35 GGUF. 3.4x smaller than the 55.6 GB bf16 safetensors the same model ships as, and it loads without re-quantizing.
